# Placetta license guides (full text)

Updated 2026-10-07. Source: https://placetta.com/guides/. General information, not legal advice; check each agency's page before filing.

## Answers
### How do I get an EIN without an SSN or ITIN?
File Form SS-4 by fax or mail, or call the IRS international line; applying online needs an SSN or ITIN. On line 7b, a responsible party with neither writes "Foreign". By fax it takes about 4 business days, by mail about 4 to 5 weeks. The IRS charges nothing; sites that charge for an EIN are resellers. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/get-an-ein-without-an-ssn.html

### How long does it take to get an EIN?
With an SSN or ITIN, online, it's issued right away. Without one: about 4 business days by fax, about 4 to 5 weeks by mail, and on the call if you phone the IRS international line. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/how-long-does-an-ein-take.html

### Does a foreign-owned single-member LLC have to file Form 5472?
Yes, every year, attached to a pro forma Form 1120 by the tax return due date. It can't be filed electronically for a disregarded entity, and the penalty for not filing starts at $25,000. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/form-5472-foreign-owned-llc.html

### Do I still need to file a beneficial ownership report (BOIR)?
Only if the company was formed outside the US and registered to do business in a US state. Since March 2025, US-formed companies are exempt. It's free, filed online, and due 30 days after the state registration takes effect. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/do-i-need-to-file-a-boir.html

### How do I become an importer of record in the US?
Get an EIN, create your importer identity with CBP Form 5106 (usually through your customs broker), buy a customs bond (CBP Form 301) from a CBP-approved surety, and open an ACE portal account to see your entries, duties and bond. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/become-an-importer-of-record.html

### Does my business need FDA food facility registration?
Yes if it makes, packs or holds food for US consumption, including facilities abroad. Restaurants and retail food stores are exempt. It's free, filed online, and renewed between October 1 and December 31 of every even-numbered year. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/fda-food-facility-registration.html

### Do I need to register cosmetics with the FDA?
Under MoCRA, the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics registers it (Form FDA 5066, every two years), and the brand on the label lists each product (Form FDA 5067, updated every year). Both are free and filed in Cosmetics Direct. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/register-cosmetics-with-the-fda.html

### Do imported consumer products need a certificate of conformity?
Yes, for products covered by CPSC rules. The importer issues the certificate itself; there is no government form. Under the eFiling rule, the certificate data is filed with CBP at entry. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/certificate-of-conformity-for-imports.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in New York City?
Across the 10 filings a restaurant in New York City makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $554.60; 3 more depend on the space or business and 3 are free. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/nyc-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in Los Angeles?
Across the 9 filings a restaurant in Los Angeles makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $870; 4 more depend on the space or business and 3 are free. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/los-angeles-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in Houston?
Across the 10 filings a restaurant in Houston makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $325; 4 more depend on the space or business and 4 are free. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/houston-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### Who needs a Food Protection Certificate in New York City?
Every food service establishment: a certified supervisor must be on site whenever you're open. The course is free online; the exam is taken in person. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/nyc-food-protection-certificate.html

### Do I need a seller's permit in California?
Yes, before your first sale, with one permit for each location. Registration is online and free, though CDTFA may ask for a security deposit. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/california-sellers-permit.html

### When do I need a sales tax Certificate of Authority in New York?
Apply through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. It's free, usually takes about two weeks, and the certificate is displayed at each location. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/new-york-certificate-of-authority.html

### Does a foreign company need to register for VAT in the UK?
Yes, from its first UK sale: a business not established in the UK has no threshold. UK-established businesses register once taxable turnover passes £90,000 in 12 months. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/uk-vat-for-foreign-companies.html

### How do I register a food business in the UK?
Register with your local council at least 28 days before opening. It's free; the council inspects and gives a food hygiene rating. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/uk-food-business-registration.html

### How do I get a trade licence in Dubai?
For a mainland business, reserve the trade name, get initial approval, then issue the licence online through Invest in Dubai. Free zone companies license through their own free zone authority instead. It renews every year. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/dubai-trade-licence.html

### Does a foreign company need a MISA license in Saudi Arabia?
Yes. A foreign-owned business gets the investment license from the Ministry of Investment before its commercial registration, and renews it with the commercial registration. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/saudi-arabia-misa-license.html

### How does a foreign company open a business in China?
Register with the local Administration for Market Regulation on the city's one-stop portal, which also sets up tax, social insurance and the company seal. The foreign investment information report goes through the same registration, and the foreign shareholder's documents need notarization and legalization or an apostille. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/open-a-company-in-china-as-a-foreigner.html

### Do I need a food business license in China?
Yes to make or serve food: apply online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead. The license is valid for 5 years. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/china-food-business-license.html

## City guides
### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in New York City
https://placetta.com/guides/new-york-city/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (New York LLC), New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Filed online with the Department of State, or mailed. Fee: $200. https://dos.ny.gov/limited-liability-company-articles-organization
3. LLC publication within 120 days, New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Publish a notice in two newspapers chosen by the county clerk for six weeks, then file the certificate with the affidavits. Fee: $50. https://dos.ny.gov/certificate-publication-domestic-limited-liability-company-0
4. Certificate of Occupancy for the use, NYC Department of Buildings. Check the space's existing CO allows your use; a change of use needs an alteration filing and an amended CO. Fee: Varies. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/certificate-of-occupancy.page
5. Application for Registration as a Sales Tax Vendor (Certificate of Authority), New York State Department of Taxation and Finance. Apply online through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. Display the certificate at each location. Fee: Free. https://www.businessexpress.ny.gov/
6. New employer registration for unemployment insurance and withholding, New York State Department of Labor. Register online once you pay wages in New York. Fee: Free. https://dol.ny.gov/register-unemployment-insurance-0
7. Proof of workers' comp and disability/paid family leave insurance, New York State Workers' Compensation Board. Buy the policies from an insurer; the insurer reports coverage to the Board. Agencies ask for the certificates. Fee: Varies. https://www.wcb.ny.gov/content/main/coverage-requirements.jsp
8. Food Protection Certificate (course and exam), NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Free online course, then an in-person exam. A certified supervisor must be on site whenever you are open. Fee: $24.60. https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/business/health-academy/food-protection-online-free.page
9. Food Service Establishment Permit, NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Apply on NYC Business. The Health Department inspects before issuing; letter grades follow. Fee: $280. https://nyc-business.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/description/food-service-establishment-permit
10. Sign permit, NYC Department of Buildings. Filed in DOB NOW by a registered design professional or licensed sign hanger. Fee: Varies. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/sign-permit.page

### Cosmetics stores in New York City
https://placetta.com/guides/new-york-city/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (New York LLC), New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Filed online with the Department of State, or mailed. Fee: $200. https://dos.ny.gov/limited-liability-company-articles-organization
3. LLC publication within 120 days, New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Publish a notice in two newspapers chosen by the county clerk for six weeks, then file the certificate with the affidavits. Fee: $50. https://dos.ny.gov/certificate-publication-domestic-limited-liability-company-0

5. Application for Registration as a Sales Tax Vendor (Certificate of Authority), New York State Department of Taxation and Finance. Apply online through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. Display the certificate at each location. Fee: Free. https://www.businessexpress.ny.gov/
6. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
7. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
8. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
10. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
11. New employer registration for unemployment insurance and withholding, New York State Department of Labor. Register online once you pay wages in New York. Fee: Free. https://dol.ny.gov/register-unemployment-insurance-0
12. Proof of workers' comp and disability/paid family leave insurance, New York State Workers' Compensation Board. Buy the policies from an insurer; the insurer reports coverage to the Board. Agencies ask for the certificates. Fee: Varies. https://www.wcb.ny.gov/content/main/coverage-requirements.jsp
13. Sign permit, NYC Department of Buildings. Filed in DOB NOW by a registered design professional or licensed sign hanger. Fee: Varies. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/sign-permit.page

### Toy stores in New York City
https://placetta.com/guides/new-york-city/toy-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (New York LLC), New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Filed online with the Department of State, or mailed. Fee: $200. https://dos.ny.gov/limited-liability-company-articles-organization
3. LLC publication within 120 days, New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Publish a notice in two newspapers chosen by the county clerk for six weeks, then file the certificate with the affidavits. Fee: $50. https://dos.ny.gov/certificate-publication-domestic-limited-liability-company-0
4. Certificate of Occupancy for the use, NYC Department of Buildings. Check the space's existing CO allows your use; a change of use needs an alteration filing and an amended CO. Fee: Varies. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/certificate-of-occupancy.page
5. Application for Registration as a Sales Tax Vendor (Certificate of Authority), New York State Department of Taxation and Finance. Apply online through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. Display the certificate at each location. Fee: Free. https://www.businessexpress.ny.gov/
6. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
7. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. New employer registration for unemployment insurance and withholding, New York State Department of Labor. Register online once you pay wages in New York. Fee: Free. https://dol.ny.gov/register-unemployment-insurance-0
10. Proof of workers' comp and disability/paid family leave insurance, New York State Workers' Compensation Board. Buy the policies from an insurer; the insurer reports coverage to the Board. Agencies ask for the certificates. Fee: Varies. https://www.wcb.ny.gov/content/main/coverage-requirements.jsp
11. Sign permit, NYC Department of Buildings. Filed in DOB NOW by a registered design professional or licensed sign hanger. Fee: Varies. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/sign-permit.page

8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Los Angeles
https://placetta.com/guides/los-angeles/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. City of Los Angeles business tax registration, City of Los Angeles Office of Finance. Register online within 30 days of starting business in the city. Fee: Varies. https://finance.lacity.gov/register-new-business
5. Food facility plan check, Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Submit plans before building out; approval comes before the public health permit. Fee: Varies. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/i-want-to/submit-electronic-plan.htm
6. Building permit and Certificate of Occupancy, Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety. Tenant improvements and changes of use go through plan check; a new use gets a new Certificate of Occupancy. Fee: Varies. https://dbs.lacity.gov/services/plan-review-permitting/building-permits
7. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
8. Public health permit (food facility), Los Angeles County Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. Apply after plan approval and before opening; an inspector visits first. Fee: Varies. http://publichealth.lacounty.gov/eh/docs/permit/Public-Health-Permit-License-Application.pdf
9. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

12. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
13. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Toy stores in Los Angeles
https://placetta.com/guides/los-angeles/toy-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. City of Los Angeles business tax registration, City of Los Angeles Office of Finance. Register online within 30 days of starting business in the city. Fee: Varies. https://finance.lacity.gov/register-new-business
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
9. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

11. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

10. Fire permits for high-piled storage and hazardous materials, Los Angeles Fire Department, Fire Prevention Bureau. Needed when storage or batteries cross fire code thresholds; inspected before issue. Fee: Varies. https://lafd.org/operational-fire-permits
11. Hazardous materials business plan, Los Angeles Fire Department CUPA. Filed in the California Environmental Reporting System when stored materials reach reporting amounts. Fee: Varies. https://lafd.org/fire-prevention/cupa/hazardous-materials

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Houston
https://placetta.com/guides/houston/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Food establishment plan review, Houston Health Department. Submit plans before building or remodeling a food establishment. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonhealth.org/food-permits/opening-food-establishment
6. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. Needed for a new tenant use or change of use inside city limits. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1106
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Food dealer permit, Houston Health Department. The operating permit, issued after plan review and inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hhd1003
9. Sign permit, City of Houston, Sign Administration. Filed with the Houston Permitting Center before the sign goes up. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1112
10. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. Needed for a new tenant use or change of use inside city limits. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1106
9. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
10. Sign permit, City of Houston, Sign Administration. Filed with the Houston Permitting Center before the sign goes up. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1112
11. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Importers and online sellers in Houston
https://placetta.com/guides/houston/importer-ecommerce.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. 5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

9. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
11. Fire permits for hazardous materials and high-piled storage, Houston Fire Department, Fire Marshal's Office. Needed when storage or batteries cross fire code thresholds. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstontx.gov/fire/formsandpermits
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Beijing
https://placetta.com/guides/beijing/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Beijing's one-stop portal, Beijing e-Window (e窗通). Beijing's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://ect.scjgj.beijing.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

### Hot pot restaurants in Shanghai
https://placetta.com/guides/shanghai/hot-pot-restaurant.html
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Shanghai's one-stop portal, Shanghai One-Window business portal (一窗通). Shanghai's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://yct.sh.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn

1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Shenzhen's one-stop portal, Shenzhen Administration for Market Regulation. Shenzhen's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://amr.sz.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Customs registration for importers and exporters, General Administration of Customs. Filed online through the China International Trade Single Window. The separate foreign trade operator filing was abolished in 2022. Fee: Free. https://www.singlewindow.cn

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Guangzhou
https://placetta.com/guides/guangzhou/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Guangzhou's one-stop portal, Guangdong Government Services (广东政务服务网). Guangzhou's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://www.gdzwfw.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

https://placetta.com/guides/hangzhou/retail-store.html
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Hangzhou's one-stop portal, Zhejiang Government Services (浙里办). Hangzhou's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://www.zjzwfw.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

https://placetta.com/guides/nanjing/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Nanjing's one-stop portal, Jiangsu Government Services. Nanjing's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://www.jszwfw.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Customs registration for importers and exporters, General Administration of Customs. Filed online through the China International Trade Single Window. The separate foreign trade operator filing was abolished in 2022. Fee: Free. https://www.singlewindow.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Xi'an's one-stop portal, Shaanxi Government Services. Xi'an's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://zwfw.shaanxi.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in London
https://placetta.com/guides/london/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Company incorporation, Companies House. Filed online with Companies House. Every director and person with significant control must verify their identity first. Fee: Varies. https://www.gov.uk/limited-company-formation/register-your-company
2. VAT registration, HM Revenue & Customs. Required once taxable turnover passes £90,000 in 12 months. A business not established in the UK registers from its first UK sale. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/register-for-vat
3. Employer registration (PAYE), HM Revenue & Customs. Register before the first payday; it can take up to 5 working days to get the employer reference. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/register-employer
4. Food business registration, Local council environmental health. Register with the local council at least 28 days before opening. It's free, and the council inspects and gives a food hygiene rating. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/food-business-registration
5. Premises licence (alcohol or late-night hot food), Local council licensing. Needed only to sell alcohol, or hot food and drink between 11pm and 5am. Fee: Varies. https://www.gov.uk/premises-licence

3. Employer registration (PAYE), HM Revenue & Customs. Register before the first payday; it can take up to 5 working days to get the employer reference. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/register-employer

1. Company creation (one-stop formalities portal), INPI, Guichet unique. All company creations are filed online here; the registration gives the SIREN and SIRET numbers and the intra-EU VAT number follows from the tax office. Fee: Varies. https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
2. Business tax account and VAT, Direction générale des Finances publiques. Open the professional space to file and pay VAT and business taxes online. Fee: Free. https://www.impots.gouv.fr/professionnel
3. Food establishment declaration, Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP). Declared online before opening, for any business that prepares, handles or stores food of animal origin. Fee: Free. https://mesdemarches.agriculture.gouv.fr

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Berlin
https://placetta.com/guides/berlin/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Commercial register entry (GmbH), Local court (Registergericht), through a notary. The articles are notarized and the notary files the registration electronically. Fee: Varies. https://www.handelsregister.de
2. Transparency register (beneficial owners), Bundesanzeiger Verlag, Transparency Register. Companies record their beneficial owners online. Fee: Varies. https://www.transparenzregister.de
3. Trade registration, Bezirksamt Berlin, Ordnungsamt. Every shop, restaurant and trading business registers its trade with Berlin before starting. The city passes it on to the tax office and the food inspectors. Fee: Varies. https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/121921/
4. Tax registration questionnaire, Finanzamt (through ELSTER). Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then issues the tax number and VAT ID. Fee: Free. https://www.elster.de

2. Transparency register (beneficial owners), Bundesanzeiger Verlag, Transparency Register. Companies record their beneficial owners online. Fee: Varies. https://www.transparenzregister.de
3. Trade registration, Landeshauptstadt München, Kreisverwaltungsreferat. Every shop, restaurant and trading business registers its trade with Munich before starting. The city passes it on to the tax office and the food inspectors. Fee: Varies. https://stadt.muenchen.de
4. Tax registration questionnaire, Finanzamt (through ELSTER). Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then issues the tax number and VAT ID. Fee: Free. https://www.elster.de

1. Company creation (CIRCE), Ministerio de Economía, CIRCE / PAE. A limited company (SL) can be created online through CIRCE with the single electronic document. Fee: Varies. https://paeelectronico.es
2. Tax census declaration, Agencia Tributaria. Registers the business for VAT and income tax before it starts trading. Fee: Free. https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
3. Employer registration with Social Security, Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social. Register as an employer and sign up each worker before they start. Fee: Free. https://sede.seg-social.gob.es
4. Opening licence or responsible declaration, Ayuntamiento de Madrid. Most shops and restaurants open with a responsible declaration filed online; larger works need a licence. Fee: Varies. https://sede.madrid.es

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Milan
https://placetta.com/guides/milan/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Business register and VAT number (ComUnica), Registro delle Imprese, Camera di Commercio. One online filing registers the company with the Chamber of Commerce, opens the VAT number and notifies social security. Fee: Varies. https://www.registroimprese.it
2. VAT number, Agenzia delle Entrate. Opened through ComUnica or directly with the tax agency before trading. Fee: Free. https://www.agenziaentrate.gov.it
3. Notice to start the activity (SCIA), Comune di Milano, SUAP. Shops and restaurants in Milan file the SCIA with the city's business desk (SUAP) before opening; restaurants add the health notice. Fee: Varies. https://www.comune.milano.it

1. Business register and VAT number (ComUnica), Registro delle Imprese, Camera di Commercio. One online filing registers the company with the Chamber of Commerce, opens the VAT number and notifies social security. Fee: Varies. https://www.registroimprese.it
2. VAT number, Agenzia delle Entrate. Opened through ComUnica or directly with the tax agency before trading. Fee: Free. https://www.agenziaentrate.gov.it
3. Notice to start the activity (SCIA), Roma Capitale, SUAP. Shops and restaurants in Rome file the SCIA with the city's business desk (SUAP) before opening; restaurants add the health notice. Fee: Varies. https://www.comune.roma.it

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Amsterdam
https://placetta.com/guides/amsterdam/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Business register (KVK), Kamer van Koophandel (KVK). Register with KVK before starting; a BV is registered by a notary. Sole traders get their VAT number from the tax office automatically. Fee: Varies. https://www.kvk.nl
2. Tax and VAT registration, Belastingdienst. Companies and foreign businesses register with the tax office for VAT and payroll tax. Fee: Free. https://www.belastingdienst.nl
3. Hospitality operating permit, Gemeente Amsterdam. Restaurants and cafes need the city's operating permit; with alcohol, an alcohol licence too. Fee: Varies. https://www.amsterdam.nl

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Dubai
https://placetta.com/guides/dubai/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Dubai trade licence, Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism. Reserve the trade name, get initial approval, then issue the licence online through Invest in Dubai. Free zones license through their own authority instead. Fee: Varies. https://invest.dubai.ae
2. Corporate tax and VAT registration, Federal Tax Authority. Every company registers for corporate tax on EmaraTax. VAT registration is required once taxable supplies pass AED 375,000 a year. Fee: Free. https://eservices.tax.gov.ae
3. Employer registration and work permits, Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Register the establishment, then apply for each employee's work permit. Fee: Varies. https://www.mohre.gov.ae
4. Food establishment approval, Dubai Municipality, Food Safety. Food businesses get the municipality's layout approval and inspection before the licence is activated. Fee: Varies. https://www.dm.gov.ae

2. Corporate tax and VAT registration, Federal Tax Authority. Every company registers for corporate tax on EmaraTax. VAT registration is required once taxable supplies pass AED 375,000 a year. Fee: Free. https://eservices.tax.gov.ae
3. Employer registration and work permits, Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Register the establishment, then apply for each employee's work permit. Fee: Varies. https://www.mohre.gov.ae

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Riyadh
https://placetta.com/guides/riyadh/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Foreign investment license, Ministry of Investment (MISA). A foreign-owned business gets the investment license before the commercial registration. Fee: Varies. https://misa.gov.sa
2. Commercial registration, Ministry of Commerce, Saudi Business Center. Registered online through the Saudi Business Center. Fee: Varies. https://business.sa
3. Tax, VAT and zakat registration, Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA). Register for zakat or income tax, and for VAT once taxable supplies pass SAR 375,000 a year. E-invoicing applies. Fee: Free. https://zatca.gov.sa
4. Social insurance employer registration, General Organization for Social Insurance. Register as an employer and enroll each employee. Fee: Free. https://www.gosi.gov.sa
5. Municipal license, Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs and Housing (Balady). Every shop, restaurant and warehouse gets the municipal license for its premises online. Fee: Varies. https://balady.gov.sa
6. Civil Defense safety license, General Directorate of Civil Defense. Premises open to the public and warehouses get the safety license online. Fee: Varies. https://998.gov.sa

3. Tax, VAT and zakat registration, Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA). Register for zakat or income tax, and for VAT once taxable supplies pass SAR 375,000 a year. E-invoicing applies. Fee: Free. https://zatca.gov.sa
4. Social insurance employer registration, General Organization for Social Insurance. Register as an employer and enroll each employee. Fee: Free. https://www.gosi.gov.sa

https://placetta.com/guides/istanbul/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Company registration (MERSIS), Ministry of Trade, Central Registry. Prepare the articles in MERSIS, then register with the trade registry. Fee: Varies. https://mersis.gtb.gov.tr
2. Tax registration, Revenue Administration (GİB). The tax office records the company and issues the tax number. Fee: Varies. https://www.gib.gov.tr
3. Business opening and operating license, Istanbul district municipality. Shops and restaurants get the opening license from their district municipality, many through e-Devlet. Fee: Varies. https://www.turkiye.gov.tr

3. Business opening and operating license, Istanbul district municipality. Shops and restaurants get the opening license from their district municipality, many through e-Devlet. Fee: Varies. https://www.turkiye.gov.tr

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Francisco
https://placetta.com/guides/san-francisco/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. San Francisco business registration, San Francisco Treasurer and Tax Collector. Register within 15 days of starting business in the city; food businesses also get a health permit from the Department of Public Health. Fee: Varies. https://sftreasurer.org
5. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
6. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Cosmetics stores in San Francisco
https://placetta.com/guides/san-francisco/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. San Francisco business registration, San Francisco Treasurer and Tax Collector. Register within 15 days of starting business in the city; food businesses also get a health permit from the Department of Public Health. Fee: Varies. https://sftreasurer.org
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
12. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
13. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

5. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
6. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

### Cosmetics stores in San Jose
https://placetta.com/guides/san-jose/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. San Jose business tax certificate, City of San Jose, Finance Department. Register for the city business tax; food businesses also get a Santa Clara County health permit. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanjoseca.gov
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
12. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
13. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Chicago
https://placetta.com/guides/chicago/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Illinois Secretary of State. Form the LLC online, or register a company formed in another state to do business in Illinois. Fee: $150. https://www.ilsos.gov
3. Sales tax registration, Illinois Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax before the first sale. Fee: Free. https://mytax.illinois.gov
4. Chicago business license, City of Chicago, Business Affairs and Consumer Protection. Most shops and restaurants need a city business license; food businesses also pass a health inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/bacp.html

6. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
7. Chicago business license, City of Chicago, Business Affairs and Consumer Protection. Most shops and restaurants need a city business license; food businesses also pass a health inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/bacp.html

### Importers and online sellers in Chicago
https://placetta.com/guides/chicago/importer-ecommerce.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Illinois Secretary of State. Form the LLC online, or register a company formed in another state to do business in Illinois. Fee: $150. https://www.ilsos.gov
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Sales tax registration, Illinois Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax before the first sale. Fee: Free. https://mytax.illinois.gov
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

2. LLC formation, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Corporations Division. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $500. https://www.sec.state.ma.us
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Sales tax registration, Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Register for sales tax and withholding before trading. Fee: Free. https://mtc.dor.state.ma.us
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
7. Boston business certificate, City of Boston, City Clerk. Anyone doing business in Boston files a business certificate; food businesses also get a permit from Inspectional Services. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov

6. ACE Secure Data Portal account for importers, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Applied for online in ACE. Lets you see your entries, duties and bond. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/getting-started/portal-applying
7. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
8. Boston business certificate, City of Boston, City Clerk. Anyone doing business in Boston files a business certificate; food businesses also get a permit from Inspectional Services. Fee: Varies. https://www.boston.gov

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Dallas
https://placetta.com/guides/dallas/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certificate of occupancy, City of Dallas, Development Services. Needed for a new business in a space; food businesses also get a food establishment permit. Fee: Varies. https://dallascityhall.com
6. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
7. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certificate of occupancy, City of Dallas, Development Services. Needed for a new business in a space; food businesses also get a food establishment permit. Fee: Varies. https://dallascityhall.com
6. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
7. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Cosmetics stores in Dallas
https://placetta.com/guides/dallas/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Certificate of occupancy, City of Dallas, Development Services. Needed for a new business in a space; food businesses also get a food establishment permit. Fee: Varies. https://dallascityhall.com
11. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

6. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
7. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Cosmetics stores in Austin
https://placetta.com/guides/austin/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Certificate of occupancy, City of Austin, Development Services. Needed for a new use of a space; food businesses also get a permit from Austin Public Health. Fee: Varies. https://www.austintexas.gov
11. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Cosmetics stores in Atlanta
https://placetta.com/guides/atlanta/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Georgia Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ecorp.sos.ga.gov
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Sales tax registration, Georgia Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax online. Fee: Free. https://gtc.dor.ga.gov
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Office of Revenue. Businesses in city limits get the city business license after zoning approval. Fee: Varies. https://www.atlantaga.gov

https://placetta.com/guides/las-vegas/hot-pot-restaurant.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation and state business license, Nevada Secretary of State (SilverFlume). Form the company and get the state business license together online. Fee: Varies. https://www.nvsilverflume.gov
3. Las Vegas business license, City of Las Vegas, Business Licensing. Get the city or Clark County business license, depending on where the store is. Fee: Varies. https://www.lasvegasnevada.gov
4. Food establishment permit, Southern Nevada Health District. Plan review, then the health permit before opening. Fee: Varies. https://www.southernnevadahealthdistrict.org
